form.name: FLW 1. The programme and your role

learn_module.name: FLW 1. The programme and your role
learn_module.description: The whole programme journey, your role and the enumerator's, what is paid and not paid, what happens outside the app, and working your record list.

fields.label:
**FLW 1. The programme and your role**

In this programme you work with very poor women and their households for about 12 months. You go back to the same women, savings groups and business groups again and again.

This lesson shows the whole journey, what is paid, and how to use your record list.

**The journey, part 1: finding households**

- You walk the community and record landmarks, businesses and the market.
- Dimagi staff import the household registry into the app. You do not do this.
- You host a community validation meeting.
- You do eligibility visits at households.

**The journey, part 2: joining**

- The government makes the final selection. You do not choose who joins.
- You enroll the selected women.
- You do onboarding with each woman.
- The enumerator does the baseline survey with each woman.

**The journey, part 3: the 12 months**

- Each woman joins a Business Savings Group, and you run its weekly sessions.
- You do a home visit with each woman every month.
- Women form business groups. Each group gets a grant in two tranches.
- The enumerator does verification visits with each business group.
- At month 12 the enumerator does the endline survey and the graduation decision.

**The enumerator works separately**

The enumerator is independent from you. She does the baseline, the business verification visits, the endline and the graduation decision. She does not coach.

You do not do her surveys, and she does not do your visits.

**A woman's status**

Each woman's record shows one of these statuses:

- **Enrolled**: set at the enrollment visit.
- **Exited**: set only in the exit section of a home visit.
- **Graduated** or **Not graduated**: set only in the endline's outcome field, by the enumerator.

**What is paid**

Paid visits include:

- an eligibility visit that is completed
- a group session: one per group per day
- a routine home visit: one per woman per scheduled month
- a targeted home visit, when the woman has an open trigger

Ask your supervisor if you are not sure whether something is paid.

Placeholder: the payment rate for each paid activity will come from KADSIPA and Dimagi.

**What is not paid**

These are part of your work, but they are not paid:

- forming a savings group
- forming a business group
- the business plan and the group agreement
- an escalation or a referral
- a home visit that finds she has left

Do them well anyway. They protect the women and the programme.

**Repeating a visit**

Check the record before you repeat a visit:

- A second routine home visit with the same woman in the same month is not paid.
- A second session with the same group on the same day is not paid.

**What happens outside this app**

Other people handle these, outside this app:

- bank accounts and money transfers
- grants
- the government's final selection
- supervision by the LGA coordinators
- grievances (complaints)

You may see some of this information in the app, but you do not manage it.

**Your record list**

The app keeps a list of records: women, households and groups. You only see the records for your own place. You come back to the same records every month.

**Finding a record**

Open the menu for the visit you are doing. Look through the list, or search for the name, to find the woman, household or group.

Check the name and details with the person in front of you before you start.

**Which visit is due**

The record list helps you see which visit is due for each woman or group. Read it before you go, so you know what to do at the visit.

**When a record is missing**

If a woman, household or group is not in your list, do not create a new record. A new record makes a duplicate. Tell your supervisor.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
A woman you work with is not in your record list. What do you do?

options.label: Create a new record for her
Tell your supervisor, and do not create a new record
Use another woman's record for now

fields.label: **Correct.** Never create a second record for the same person. Tell your supervisor.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** if a record is missing, do not create a new one, because that makes a duplicate. Tell your supervisor.
Which of these visits is NOT paid?

options.label: A home visit that finds she has left
A completed eligibility visit
A routine home visit in her scheduled month

fields.label: **Correct.** A home visit that finds she has left is not paid.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a home visit that finds she has left is not paid. A completed eligibility visit and a routine home visit in her scheduled month are paid.
Who does the baseline survey with each woman?

options.label: You, the FLW
Your LGA coordinator
The enumerator

fields.label: **Correct.** The enumerator does the baseline, separately from you.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** the enumerator does the baseline survey. She works independently from you.

learn_module.name: FLW 2. Consent and privacy
learn_module.description: Eligibility consent versus participation consent, refusals and declines, and asking sensitive questions in private.

fields.label:
**FLW 2. Consent and privacy**

Every person decides for herself whether to take part. This lesson covers the two kinds of consent, what to do when someone says no, and how to ask private questions.

**Two kinds of consent**

- At the **eligibility visit**, the household agrees to answer the eligibility questions.
- At **enrollment**, each woman agrees to take part in the programme.

Agreeing to the eligibility visit is not agreeing to join.

**Asking for consent**

Read the consent words in the app clearly. Give time for questions. Do not push. A person can say no, and saying no is fine.

**When a household refuses the eligibility visit**

Record the refusal and leave politely. Do not argue, and do not come back to push them.

**When a woman declines to join**

At enrollment, a woman may decline. Record the decline on the household's record. Leave your phone number and the complaints number with her, in case she has questions later.

Placeholder: the complaints (grievance) number and how it works will come from KADSIPA.

**Ask sensitive questions in private**

Some questions are sensitive, for example about money or about safety at home. Ask them privately, away from other adults, including her husband and in-laws.

Ask politely if you can speak with her alone, for example outside or in another room.

**Keep her answers private**

Do not tell other people what she answered, not even her family or neighbours.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
The household agreed to the eligibility visit. At enrollment, does each woman still give her own consent?

options.label: No, the household already agreed
Only if her husband agrees first
Yes, each woman gives her own consent

fields.label: **Correct.** Eligibility consent and participation consent are different. Each woman gives her own consent at enrollment.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** agreeing to the eligibility visit is not agreeing to join. At enrollment, each woman gives her own consent.
A woman declines to join at enrollment. What do you do?

options.label: Record the decline on the household, and leave your number and the complaints number
Come back next week and ask her again
Ask her husband to talk to her about joining

fields.label: **Correct.** Record the decline, leave your phone number and the complaints number, and respect her choice.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** record the decline on the household's record, and leave your phone number and the complaints number. Respect her choice.
You need to ask a sensitive question. Her mother-in-law is sitting with you. What do you do?

options.label: Ask quietly so the mother-in-law does not hear
Ask politely to speak with her alone first
Ask the mother-in-law to answer for her

fields.label: **Correct.** Ask sensitive questions privately, away from other adults.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** ask sensitive questions privately, away from other adults. Ask politely to speak with her alone.

form.name: FLW 3. Community walk and validation meeting

learn_module.name: FLW 3. Community walk and validation meeting
learn_module.description: The community walk, the market survey and hosting the community validation meeting.

fields.label:
**FLW 3. Community walk and validation meeting**

Before households are visited, you get to know the community. Then you host a meeting where the community checks the household list.

**The community walk**

Walk through the community. Record the landmarks, the businesses and the market. This helps everyone find households later.

**The market survey**

At the market, you answer a short market survey in the app.

Placeholder: the market survey questions will come from KADSIPA.

**Hosting the validation meeting**

Invite community members and leaders. Explain what the programme is and how the meeting works. Keep the meeting calm and respectful.

**Explaining the selection criteria**

Explain the selection criteria in general words. Never share any household's details at the meeting: not their answers, and not their situation.

Placeholder: the wording of the selection criteria will come from KADSIPA.

**Recording each household**

For each household on the list, record what the community says:

- **Confirmed**, or
- **Objection**, with the reason the community gives.

Write the reason as the community said it.

**Households that were missed**

The community may name households that are not on the list. Record each one with enough detail to find it: the name, where it is, and a landmark near it.

Do not add your own opinion about the household.

**The women's breakout**

Hold a separate breakout with the women. Women may speak more freely there. Record what they say in the same way: confirmed, objection with a reason, or a missed household.

**Complaints go to the grievance channel**

If someone wants to complain about the programme or the selection, tell them about the grievance channel. The grievance channel is separate from you. You do not decide complaints.

Placeholder: the grievance channel details will come from KADSIPA.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
At the meeting, someone asks why a certain household is on the list. What do you do?

options.label: Show them that household's answers so they understand
Tell them what you know about that household's situation
Explain the criteria in general words, without that household's details

fields.label: **Correct.** Explain the criteria in general words. Never share a household's details.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** explain the selection criteria in general words, and never share any household's details at the meeting.
A neighbour names a household that was missed. You think it is not very poor. What do you record?

options.label: The household, with your opinion that it is not poor
The household, with enough detail to find it, and no opinion of yours
Nothing, because you think it is not poor

fields.label: **Correct.** Record the missed household with enough detail to find it. Do not add your own view.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** record every missed household the community names, with enough detail to find it, and without your own view.
Someone at the meeting is angry about the selection and wants to complain. What do you do?

options.label: Tell them about the grievance channel
Decide the complaint yourself after the meeting
Promise to add their household to the list

fields.label: **Correct.** Complaints go to the grievance channel, which is separate from you.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** you do not decide complaints. Tell the person about the grievance channel, which is separate from you.

learn_module.name: FLW 4. Eligibility visit
learn_module.description: Recording the visit outcome, payment for completed visits only, consent and roster, neutral questions and the hidden score.

fields.label:
**FLW 4. Eligibility visit**

At the eligibility visit, you ask a household KADSIPA's eligibility questions. The answers help the government make the final selection.

**Record the visit outcome first**

The first thing you record is what happened:

- **Completed**: you did the visit
- **Not found**: you could not find the household
- **Refused**: the household said no

**Only a completed visit is paid**

Only an eligibility visit with the outcome Completed is paid. A visit where the household is not found, or refuses, is recorded but not paid.

Always record the true outcome.

**Consent and the household roster**

Ask for consent for the eligibility visit. Then record the household roster: the list of household members, as the app asks.

**Ask the questions neutrally**

Read each question as it is written. Do not hint at a good or bad answer. Do not skip questions or change the words. Ask every household in the same way.

**The eligibility questions**

Placeholder: KADSIPA's eligibility tool questions and its scoring will come from KADSIPA.

**You never see the score**

The phone works out the eligibility score. The score is never shown to you or to the household. The app never tells anyone that a household is eligible.

**If the household asks whether they will be selected**

Explain that the government makes the final selection later. Do not guess, and do not promise anything.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
You cannot find the household, even after asking neighbours. You record Not found. Is this visit paid?

options.label: Yes, because you made the trip
No, only a completed visit is paid
Yes, if you go back once more

fields.label: **Correct.** Only a completed eligibility visit is paid. Still record Not found truthfully.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** only an eligibility visit with the outcome Completed is paid. Not found and Refused are recorded but not paid.
After the questions, the household asks if they will be selected. What do you say?

options.label: Tell them they look eligible
Tell them their score from the phone
Explain that the government makes the final selection later

fields.label: **Correct.** The app never says a household is eligible, and you never see the score.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** the score is never shown to you or to the household, and nobody is told they are eligible. The government makes the final selection.

learn_module.name: FLW 5. Enrollment and onboarding
learn_module.description: Who to enroll, each woman's consent, government support, the account name, PINs and transfer problems.

fields.label:
**FLW 5. Enrollment and onboarding**

After the government's final selection, you enroll the selected households and do onboarding with each woman.

**Confirm the right household**

Before you start, check that you are at the selected household. Check the name and details in the record with the people in front of you.

**Who to enroll**

Enroll one adult woman who eats from the same pot as the household.

**Polygamous households**

In a polygamous household, enroll each adult wife who eats from the same pot.

**When there is no adult woman**

If the household has no adult woman, enroll the man.

**Each woman's own consent**

Each woman you enroll gives her own consent. Nobody can consent for her.

When she agrees and you enroll her, her status becomes **Enrolled**.

**Women who cannot attend groups**

Some women cannot attend group meetings. Flag each such woman to your supervisor.

**Government support**

Record the government support the household receives, as the app asks. You never set or change any amount.

**Confirm the account name**

Confirm with her that the account name shown in the app is her own name.

**Never ask for a PIN**

Never ask for her PIN. Never write it down or type it into your phone. If she starts to tell you, stop her kindly. Her PIN protects her money.

**Failed or reversed transfer flags**

The app may show that a transfer **failed** (the money did not reach her account) or was **reversed** (the money was taken back).

Explain this to her calmly. Do not promise when money will come. Pass her questions on to your supervisor.

**She says a transfer did not arrive**

Sometimes she says the money did not arrive, but the system shows it as sent. Then:

- record what she says
- never promise her money
- pass it on to your supervisor

**Onboarding**

At onboarding, explain how the programme will work for her: the savings group, the weekly sessions, the monthly home visits and the business grants. Answer her questions.

Placeholder: the detailed onboarding steps will come from KADSIPA.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
In a polygamous household, two adult wives eat from the same pot. Who do you enroll?

options.label: Only the first wife
Each adult wife who eats from the same pot
The husband

fields.label: **Correct.** Enroll each adult wife who eats from the same pot.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** in a polygamous household, enroll each adult wife who eats from the same pot. Enroll the man only when there is no adult woman.
She says the transfer did not arrive, but the system shows it as sent. What do you do?

options.label: Promise her the money will come next week
Tell her the system shows it was sent, so it must be there
Record what she says, pass it on, and promise nothing

fields.label: **Correct.** Record it, pass it on, and never promise money.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** record what she says, never promise money, and pass it on to your supervisor.
To help check her account, can you ask for her PIN?

options.label: No, never ask for a PIN
Yes, if she agrees
Yes, if your supervisor asks you to

fields.label: **Correct.** Never ask for a PIN, for any reason.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** never ask for a PIN, for any reason, and never write one down.

learn_module.name: FLW 6. Savings group and sessions
learn_module.description: The savings group, never handling its money, sessions, attendance, home-visit triggers and possible-exit flags.

fields.label:
**FLW 6. Savings group and sessions**

Each woman joins a savings group. You meet each group every week for a session.

**The savings group**

Members meet regularly and save together. The group agrees its own rules.

Placeholder: the details of the savings group method will come from KADSIPA's curriculum guide.

**You never handle the money**

The group runs its own cash box and its own ledger. You never hold, count, carry or keep the group's money, not even to help.

If they ask you to, kindly say no and help them choose a member to do it.

**Use the session guide**

Facilitate each session with the session guide on your phone. Follow the steps for that week. Let the members talk and decide.

Placeholder: the session guide content will come from KADSIPA's curriculum guide.

**Record attendance**

Use the tick-list in the app. Tick only the women who are really there.

**Who needs a home visit**

After the session, decide who needs a home visit.

A woman who misses **2 sessions in a row** becomes due a targeted home visit **within 7 days**.

**One paid session per group per day**

Only one session per group per day is paid. A second session with the same group on the same day is not paid.

**A session never records an exit**

If members say a woman has left, you can flag a possible exit in the session. A session never records an exit.

An exit is recorded only at a home visit, when it is confirmed there.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
The group's box keeper asks you to count the money for them. What do you do?

options.label: Count it quickly, then hand it back
Kindly say no; a member counts it and writes it in the ledger
Count it and write the amount in the ledger yourself

fields.label: **Correct.** You never handle the group's money. The group runs its own cash box and ledger.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** you never hold, count or keep the group's money. The group runs its own cash box and ledger.
A woman missed 2 sessions in a row. What is due?

options.label: A targeted home visit within 7 days
Nothing until she misses 4 sessions
Only her routine visit next month

fields.label: **Correct.** 2 missed sessions in a row makes a targeted home visit due within 7 days.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a woman who misses 2 sessions in a row becomes due a targeted home visit within 7 days.
At a session, members say a woman has moved away. What do you record in the session?

options.label: Her exit
Nothing at all
A possible exit flag

fields.label: **Correct.** A session can flag a possible exit. The exit itself is recorded only at a home visit.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a session never records an exit. Flag a possible exit; the exit is recorded only when it is confirmed at a home visit.

form.name: FLW 7. Business groups, plan and grant

learn_module.name: FLW 7. Business groups, plan and grant
learn_module.description: Self-selected business groups, the cooking stones, the agreement, the two tranches and the receipt confirmation visit.

fields.label:
**FLW 7. Business groups, plan and grant**

Women form small business groups. Each group makes a business plan and an agreement, and receives a grant in two tranches.

**Women choose their own group**

Facilitate. Let the women choose who they work with. Do not assign anyone to a group.

**The cooking stones**

Think of the stones that hold a cooking pot. The stones do not need to be the same. But each stone must be strong, and each must be placed to work with the others, or the pot falls.

A good business group is the same: members can be different, but each must be strong and work with the others.

**Guide the comparison**

Help the group compare its business ideas by asking questions. Do not choose the business for them. The decision is theirs.

Placeholder: the comparison steps will come from KADSIPA's curriculum guide.

**The business plan and the group agreement**

The group makes a business plan and a group agreement that every member understands and accepts. Forming the group, the business plan and the agreement are not paid.

Placeholder: the business plan and agreement templates will come from KADSIPA's curriculum guide.

**Two tranches**

The grant comes in two tranches. The second tranche depends on the enumerator's business verification. Verification visit 2, about 3 months after the first tranche, decides it.

Placeholder: the exact tranche conditions will come from KADSIPA.

**The receipt confirmation visit**

After a tranche, you visit the group to confirm they received it.

Ask the members to say the amount they received **before** the phone shows the expected amount. Then compare.

**If the amount is wrong**

If the amount the members state is different from the expected amount, record what they say. Do not argue, and do not promise anything. Raise an escalation.

**If someone outside the group controls the money**

If a husband, a leader or anyone outside the group is controlling the grant money, raise an escalation. Do not try to sort it out yourself.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
Two women ask you to put them in the strongest group. What do you do?

options.label: Put them in the group you think is best
Help all the women choose their own groups
Ask the community leader to assign them

fields.label: **Correct.** Women choose their own groups. You facilitate; you do not assign.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** facilitate self-selection. Do not assign anyone to a group.
At the receipt confirmation visit, when do members state the amount they received?

options.label: Before the phone shows the expected amount
After you read the expected amount to them
Only if they think the amount is wrong

fields.label: **Correct.** Members state the amount first. Then the phone shows the expected amount.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** members state the amount they received before the phone shows the expected amount.
Members say a woman's husband has taken the group's grant money. What do you do?

options.label: Go and talk to the husband to get it back
Wait a month to see if he returns it
Raise an escalation

fields.label: **Correct.** Someone outside the group controlling the money is an escalation.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** when someone outside the group controls the money, raise an escalation. Do not try to sort it out yourself.

learn_module.name: FLW 8. Home visits
learn_module.description: Routine and targeted home visits and their payment rules, the coaching agreement and the readiness review.

fields.label:
**FLW 8. Home visits**

You visit each woman at home: a routine visit every month, and a targeted visit when something needs attention.

**The monthly routine visit**

Do one routine home visit with each woman in each scheduled month. One routine visit per woman per scheduled month is paid.

A second routine visit with the same woman in the same month is not paid.

**Targeted visits**

A targeted visit is for a woman with an open trigger. For example: she missed 2 sessions in a row.

A targeted visit is paid only when she has an open trigger. Doing the visit clears the trigger.

**The first visit: the coaching agreement**

At the first home visit, make the coaching agreement with her. Help her set her own goals and make an action plan. Use her words, not yours.

**Coaching at each visit**

At each visit, look at her goals and action plan together.

Placeholder: the coaching content for each visit will come from KADSIPA's curriculum guide.

**Private questions**

Some home visit questions are private. Ask them away from other adults, including her husband and in-laws.

**The readiness review (months 9 to 10)**

Around months 9 to 10, review with her how ready she is for graduation. This is coaching: help her see her progress and what to work on.

You do not make the graduation decision. The enumerator makes it at the endline.

Placeholder: the graduation criteria will come from KADSIPA.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
You did Amina's routine visit on 5 March. On 20 March you do another routine visit with her. How many routine visits are paid for her in March?

options.label: Two, because both visits happened
One
None, because you visited twice

fields.label: **Correct.** One routine visit per woman per scheduled month is paid.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** one routine visit per woman per scheduled month is paid. A second routine visit in the same month is not paid.
A woman has no open trigger, but you want to check on her with a targeted visit. Is it paid?

options.label: No, a targeted visit is paid only with an open trigger
Yes, if you write down your reason
Yes, any targeted visit is paid

fields.label: **Correct.** A targeted visit is paid only when she has an open trigger, and the visit clears it.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a targeted visit is paid only when the woman has an open trigger. The visit clears the trigger.
At the readiness review in month 9, a woman asks if she has graduated. What do you say?

options.label: Yes, you are doing well
Not yet, you need more time
The enumerator decides at the endline; let us look at your progress

fields.label: **Correct.** The readiness review is coaching. The enumerator makes the graduation decision at the endline.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** the readiness review is coaching. The graduation decision stays with the enumerator, at the endline.

learn_module.name: FLW 9. Escalation, referral and exit
learn_module.description: Escalation categories, safeguarding, referral, and recording an exit only when it is confirmed.

fields.label:
**FLW 9. Escalation, referral and exit**

Sometimes a woman faces a serious problem, or leaves the programme. This lesson covers escalation, referral and recording an exit.

**When to escalate**

Raise an escalation in one of these categories:

- safeguarding or violence
- someone else controlling her money
- serious illness or death
- conflict over the programme
- fraud or misuse
- other

**Safeguarding: listen, do not investigate, pass on**

If a woman tells you about violence or abuse:

- **listen** calmly
- **do not investigate**: do not question other people, and do not confront anyone
- **pass it on the same day**

**Who to contact**

Placeholder: the escalation contacts and how to reach them will come from KADSIPA.

**Referral**

When a woman needs a local service, refer her to a service from the services directory.

Placeholder: the services directory will come from KADSIPA.

**Escalations and referrals are not paid**

Escalations and referrals are not paid. Do them every time they are needed. They protect the women.

**Recording an exit**

Record an exit only when it is confirmed at a home visit, in person, with the household or neighbours. Never record an exit on hearsay, for example from a group session or from someone at the market.

When you record the exit, her status becomes **Exited**.

**A visit that finds she has left is not paid**

If you go for a home visit and find that she has left, record the exit. This visit is not paid.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
A woman tells you her brother-in-law hits her. What do you do?

options.label: Talk to the brother-in-law to stop it
Listen, do not investigate, and pass it on the same day
Ask the neighbours what they have seen

fields.label: **Correct.** Listen, do not investigate, and pass it on the same day.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** for safeguarding, listen, do not investigate or confront anyone, and pass it on the same day.
Someone at the market tells you a woman has left the community. What do you do?

options.label: Do a home visit, and record an exit only if it is confirmed there
Record her exit today
Ask her savings group to record the exit

fields.label: **Correct.** Record an exit only when it is confirmed in person at a home visit.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** never record an exit on hearsay. Record it only when it is confirmed in person at a home visit.
On a home visit, her family confirms she has left for good. You record the exit. Is this visit paid?

options.label: Yes, it counts as her routine visit
Yes, because you recorded the exit
No, it is not paid

fields.label: **Correct.** A visit that finds she has left is not paid.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a home visit that finds she has left is not paid, even though you record the exit.

learn_module.name: Enumerator 1. Your role
learn_module.description: Your independence from the FLW, what is paid and not paid, and working your record list.

fields.label:
**Enumerator 1. Your role**

You collect information that shows how the women and their businesses are doing. Your work must be independent, and the same for everyone.

**Your tasks**

- the baseline survey with each woman
- three business verification visits with each business group
- the endline survey with each participant
- the graduation decision at the endline

**You are independent from the FLW**

The FLW (mentor) coaches the women. You do not coach. You do not give advice on businesses or savings.

If a woman asks you for advice, tell her to ask her FLW.

**A woman's status**

Each woman's record shows one of these statuses:

- **Enrolled**: set by the FLW at the enrollment visit
- **Exited**: set only by the FLW, in the exit section of a home visit
- **Graduated** or **Not graduated**: set only by you, in the endline's outcome field

**What is paid**

- the baseline: once per woman
- each business verification visit
- the endline: once per participant

Placeholder: the payment rates will come from KADSIPA and Dimagi.

**What is not paid**

A verification visit where the group is **not found**, or where the group **refuses**, is recorded but not paid. Always record the true outcome.

**Your record list**

You see the records of every FLW place in your area, not just one place. Your list has women and business groups from several FLWs.

**Finding a participant or group**

Open the menu for the visit you are doing. Look through the list, or search for the woman's or group's name. Check the name and details before you start.

**Which visit is due**

The record list helps you see which visit is due: the baseline, verification visit 1, 2 or 3, or the endline. Check it before you go.

**When a record is missing**

If a woman or group is not in your list, do not create a new record. A new record makes a duplicate. Tell your supervisor.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
A woman asks you how to sell more at her shop. What do you do?

options.label: Give her some quick advice
Tell her to ask her FLW
Agree to come back and coach her

fields.label: **Correct.** You do not coach. The FLW coaches.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** you are independent from the FLW and you do not coach. Send her questions to her FLW.
At a verification visit, the group cannot be found. Is the visit paid?

options.label: No, it is recorded but not paid
Yes, because you made the trip
Yes, if you searched for more than an hour

fields.label: **Correct.** Group not found is recorded but not paid.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a verification visit where the group is not found, or refuses, is recorded but not paid.
Whose records do you see in your list?

options.label: Only the records of your own place
Only one FLW's records
The records of every FLW place in your area

fields.label: **Correct.** You see the records of every FLW place in your area.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** as an enumerator, you see the records of every FLW place in your area.

learn_module.name: Enumerator 2. Consent and privacy
learn_module.description: Consent, refusals, asking each woman's section privately and recording whether privacy was possible.

fields.label:
**Enumerator 2. Consent and privacy**

Every person decides for herself whether to answer. Some of your questions are private.

**Asking for consent**

Read the consent words in the app clearly before each survey. Give time for questions. A person can say no, and that is fine.

**When someone says no**

If a woman or a group refuses, record the refusal and leave politely. Do not argue or push.

**Each woman's section is private**

Ask each woman her own section privately, away from other adults, including her husband and in-laws. Ask politely if you can speak with her alone.

**Record whether privacy was possible**

After her section, record whether you were able to ask it in private. Be honest: if others stayed, record that.

**Keep answers private**

Do not tell anyone what a woman answered, not even her family or neighbours.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
Her husband wants to listen while you ask her section. What do you do?

options.label: Let him listen
Ask him to answer for her
Ask politely to speak with her alone, and record whether privacy was possible

fields.label: **Correct.** Ask her section privately, and record whether privacy was possible.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** ask each woman her own section privately, away from other adults, and record whether privacy was possible.
After a woman's section, what do you record about privacy?

options.label: Nothing
Whether privacy was possible
The names of everyone nearby

fields.label: **Correct.** Record honestly whether privacy was possible.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** after each woman's section, record whether privacy was possible.

learn_module.name: Enumerator 3. Baseline and endline
learn_module.description: Neutral, consistent baseline and endline surveys, and never overwriting the baseline.

fields.label:
**Enumerator 3. Baseline and endline**

The baseline shows each woman's situation at the start. The endline shows it at month 12. Comparing the two shows what changed.

**Ask neutrally**

Read every question as it is written. Do not hint at a good or bad answer. Do not skip questions or change the words.

**The same way every round**

Ask the baseline and the endline in the same way, with the same words and the same care. If you change how you ask, the answers cannot be compared.

**Household section and women's sections**

Ask the household section once, for the household. Ask each woman her own section privately.

**Never overwrite the baseline**

The baseline is never changed after it is recorded. The endline is its own new record.

If something is different at the endline, record it in the endline and leave the baseline as it is.

**The survey questions**

Placeholder: the baseline (Entry survey) and endline (Exit survey) questions will come from KADSIPA when it shares its instruments.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
At the endline you find that a baseline answer was wrong. What do you do?

options.label: Correct the baseline
Leave the baseline; record today's answers in the endline
Delete the baseline and do it again

fields.label: **Correct.** The baseline is never overwritten. The endline is its own record.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** the baseline is never overwritten. Record today's answers in the endline, which is its own record.
In one survey round, how often do you ask the household section?

options.label: Once, for the household
Once for each woman
Only at the endline

fields.label: **Correct.** The household section is asked once. Each woman's own section is asked privately.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** ask the household section once, for the household, and each woman's own section privately.

learn_module.name: Enumerator 4. Business verification
learn_module.description: Timing of the three verification visits, outcomes and payment, the live photo, the clearing rule and flags for the FLW.

fields.label:
**Enumerator 4. Business verification**

You visit each business group three times to check its business. Your visits decide whether a group gets the second tranche.

**When the three visits happen**

The visits are timed from when the group receives a tranche:

- **Visit 1**: about 1 month after the first tranche
- **Visit 2**: about 3 months after the first tranche. This visit decides the second tranche.
- **Visit 3**: about 2 months after the second tranche

**Who must be there**

You can record the visit when at least one group member is present. You do not need every member.

**Not found, refused, closed**

- Group **not found**: record it. It is not paid.
- Group **refused**: record it. It is not paid.
- Business found **closed**: this is a completed visit. Record it fully. It is paid.

**The live photo**

Take a live photo, with the app's camera, of what the first tranche bought. Never use a picture from the phone's gallery. Never photograph another photo or a phone screen.

**The Business Progress Survey**

Placeholder: the Business Progress Survey questions will come from KADSIPA.

**The clearing rule**

At visit 2, the clearing rule decides whether the group is cleared for the second tranche. Apply it in the same way for every group: whether you like the group or not, and whether they worked hard or not.

Placeholder: the exact clearing rule will come from KADSIPA.

**Not cleared at visit 2**

If a group is not cleared at visit 2, it gets visit 3 about **1 month later**.

**Inactive members and possible exits**

If a member is no longer active, or may have left, flag it for the FLW. You never record an exit yourself. The FLW confirms exits at a home visit.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
Only one member is there at the verification visit. Can you record the visit?

options.label: No, all members must be there
No, at least half must be there
Yes, one member present is enough

fields.label: **Correct.** You can record the visit when at least one member is present.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a verification visit can be recorded when at least one group member is present.
You find that the group's business has closed. What is this visit?

options.label: A completed visit, and it is paid
Not found, and it is not paid
Refused, and it is not paid

fields.label: **Correct.** A business found closed is a completed, paid visit.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** a business found closed is a completed visit, and it is paid. Only not found and refused are unpaid.
Members show you a photo, on a phone, of the sewing machine they bought. What do you do?

options.label: Use that photo
Take a live photo of the sewing machine with the app's camera
Take a photo of the phone screen

fields.label: **Correct.** Always take a live photo with the app's camera.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** take a live photo of what was bought, with the app's camera. Never use a gallery image or a photo of a screen.

learn_module.name: Enumerator 5. Graduation
learn_module.description: Applying the graduation criteria consistently and recording exactly one outcome.

fields.label:
**Enumerator 5. Graduation**

At the endline, you decide whether each woman has graduated.

**Apply the criteria the same way**

Apply the graduation criteria in the same way for every woman. Do not let friendship, pity or pressure change your decision.

Placeholder: the graduation criteria will come from KADSIPA.

**Exactly one outcome**

Record exactly one outcome in the endline's outcome field:

- **Graduated**, or
- **Not graduated**

There is no extension, and there is no other choice.

**Explaining the outcome**

Explain the outcome to her calmly and respectfully, in simple words.

**Borderline cases**

If a case is close, still apply the criteria and record one outcome. A supervisor reviews borderline cases outside the app.

**Practice**

Answer these practice questions. They are not scored.
A woman is close to the criteria and asks for more time. What can you record?

options.label: An extension of 3 months
Graduated or Not graduated
Nothing until your supervisor decides

fields.label: **Correct.** There are only two outcomes, and there is no extension.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** record exactly one outcome, Graduated or Not graduated. There is no extension.
Who reviews borderline cases?

options.label: A supervisor, outside the app
The FLW, at a home visit
The woman's savings group

fields.label: **Correct.** A supervisor reviews borderline cases outside the app.
**Not quite — here is the rule:** you record one outcome; a supervisor reviews borderline cases outside the app.
